title: Hosted API enterprise eligibility sieve for chat/streaming/toolcalls/structured outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit Hosted API feature requests that span chat, streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. Current intake is noisy: many requests need compliance review, some require Dedicated/Private deployment, and others are safe for self-serve. Goal: define an eligibility 'sieve' and a lightweight scoring rubric that automatically classifies inbound requests into routing buckets (self-serve backlog, product-managed review, legal/security review, Dedicated/Private engineering intake). Deliver a clear escalation/playbook so PMs can triage enterprise requests quickly and consistently.
acceptance_criteria: Scoped rubric documented and published in Confluence
Intake form updated to capture all scoring signals programmatically
Automated classification prototype in Zapier/Sheets routes >= 80% of new enterprise requests to the correct bucket
Weekly triage cadence defined with owners and SLA for manual reviews (48 hours)
Stakeholder signoff: Legal, Security, Runtime Eng, Solutions Engineering
scoring_rubric: SLA / latency requirement (weight 30): millisecond SLO needed? high throughput? -> pushes toward Dedicated/Private
Data sensitivity (weight 30): PHI/PCI/regulated data presence -> legal/security review and likely Private
Throughput / concurrency (weight 20): sustained QPS > X or streaming sessions -> Dedicated consideration
Integration complexity (weight 10): external toolchains, callback webhooks, function chaining -> requires Solutions Eng
Business impact (weight 10): revenue-bound contract, pilot with paying customer -> escalate priority
decision_log: 2026-02-20: PM kickoff; agreed to avoid hard-blocking self-serve for non-sensitive feature asks
2026-02-27: Security reviewed preliminary rubric; requested explicit PHI/PII question in form
2026-03-05: Eng recommended SLA thresholds and suggested Dedicated as default for sustained QPS>200
2026-03-12: Finalized weight distribution (30/30/20/10/10) and approved weekly manual review slot
tradeoffs: Strict gating reduces false-positives to Dedicated but increases friction for customers and manual reviews
Loose gating speeds onboarding but risks missing compliance needs until later, increasing legal exposure
Automating classification early can reduce load but needs high-quality signals from intake form (more fields may reduce conversion)
